question: After the correctness repairs and exact-head proof, should OpenClaw sponsor this new generic app-guided provider-auth contract across the gateway, plugin manifest, CLI, and macOS onboarding?
rationale: The implementation adds a public plugin metadata capability and a new cross-client onboarding mode; code review can require correctness and compatibility, but maintainers must confirm that this broad permanent product/API surface is intended.

options.title: Sponsor after repairs
options.body: Keep the generic manifest-driven contract, require both findings and native lint to be fixed, and merge only after exact-head real behavior and upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Retain the generic seam but initially advertise only provider choices with proven credential-to-model activation and complete native proof.

options.title: Do not add this contract
options.body: Close or redesign the PR if app-guided provider authentication should not become a supported plugin and gateway surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repairs
recommendation.body: Keep the generic manifest-driven contract, require both findings and native lint to be fixed, and merge only after exact-head real behavior and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the recent merged history for verified onboarding, provider catalog integration, gateway lease handling, and the affected activation invariant.
